CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

H-RESPONSE-SPEED.statement: The August dispute surge is primarily a ticket-handling/response-speed problem (slow or inconsistent CS replies), not an underlying billing-data error.

H-AMI-READ-FAILURE.statement: A change or fault in AMI meter read delivery/validation (MDMS) since August is causing missing/incorrect reads, forcing bad estimate substitutions and wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-FAILURE.statement: Degraded manual field meter-reading (missed routes, staffing shortfall) since August is reducing accepted reads, driving estimate substitution and billing errors.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to billing import validation rules around August introduced a systematic bill-calculation or estimate-substitution error.

H-TICKET-REPORTING-ARTIFACT.statement: The reported doubling of dispute tickets since August is partly a measurement/categorization artifact in CRM rather than a real increase in incorrect bills.

H-TARIFF-CALC-ERROR.statement: A tariff or billing calculation/import defect — not a missing read — produces wrong bills even on accounts with an accepted ACTUAL read, explaining why most disputed bills (1785 of 3025, E-04) are ACTUAL read type.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Field route completion for manual-read accounts ran at 0.88 against a 0.95 target over Aug-Sep 2026, covering 9200 manual-read accounts (E-01). This shows a measurable but moderate shortfall in field read collection, not a wholesale breakdown.
CRM data on 2440 dispute tickets shows median response time 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days against a 3.0-day SLA — response handling is currently fast and within SLA, not slow or inconsistent (E-02).

CRM dispute volume rose from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to 1180 in Aug and 1260 in Sep 2026 (E-03), a near-doubling of raw ticket counts coincident with the reported surge. This confirms the magnitude and timing of the surge as a real increase in raw ticket counts, not merely a shift in response speed or SLA handling, but says nothing about which upstream cause (AMI, field reads, billing rules) is responsible.

Of disputed bills, 1785 (59%) carry read_type ACTUAL versus 1240 (41%) ESTIMATED (E-04), so most disputed bills were generated from a received meter read, not an estimate substitution. This weighs against estimate-substitution (AMI or field read failure) being the majority driver of the dispute surge and points toward a calculation/import issue affecting bills regardless of read source.

E-05.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead) asserts no tariff change occurred this year; as an unverified stakeholder statement (NON_AUTHORITATIVE) it only partially bears on tariff-related causal paths and does not address billing import/validation rule changes, which are a separate log.

E-06.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD (Field Operations Manager) claims the field crew has been short three readers since July, causing late routes and estimated bills for affected customers. This is an unverified stakeholder claim offering a causal mechanism consistent with the measured route-completion shortfall (E-01), but it does not quantify how much of the dispute surge this explains, and SH-FIELD has a stated incentive to attribute problems to staffing (contract headcount increase).

Billing-db's tariff_change_log returned 0 records (E-07), an authoritative, complete system-of-record check confirming no tariff change was logged this year, corroborating the prior non-authoritative claim (CL-02) and stakeholder-sourced evidence (E-05).

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Service contract §4.2 confirms the utility may request field route priority changes, but execution happens only after confirmation by the Field Operations Manager (E-08), corroborating the existing K-DISPATCH human-approval requirement on push_route_update rather than revealing anything new about the dispute-surge cause.

interpretation_history.interpretation: route-log.lagging_routes returns 14 specific routes with individual completion rates (sample: R-00 at 0.70), giving a per-route breakdown underlying the 0.88 aggregate manual-read completion rate (E-01) rather than any new causal mechanism.

E-10.content: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle → 320 record(s); fields ['account_id', 'route'] | account_id: 320 distinct values | route: 40 distinct values | sample: {"account_id": "AC-20000", "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle (E-10) shows 320 accounts received estimated bills last cycle, spanning 40 distinct routes — nearly three times the 14 routes specifically flagged as lagging (E-09). This indicates estimated-bill substitution is not confined to the routes affected by the identified field-staffing shortfall, so route lag alone does not account for the full breadth of estimation.
